participants: Ben Byrne (running the session as the coach)
summary: Not a Primal Instinct call. This is an hour-long group sales training that Ben Byrne runs for members of a separate programme belonging to someone called Boris, whose members sell marketing and advertising services to local businesses — landscapers, chiropractors, massage therapists, remodellers. Ben is the coach, not a participant. The session covers ad messaging and targeting, a law-of-attraction segment on desire and letting go of outcome, and then live Q&A on sales technique: how to pitch $6,000 without losing frame, the full open-wallet framework including credit-card questions, how to handle clients who do not do the work, and the order of logistics versus emotion in discovery. Ben discloses on the recording that he is 'back closing for Boris again' and characterises the Primal offer and its prospects in dismissive terms. He ends the session to take a Primal call.
notable: Filed in the Ben Byrne rep folder of the Primal corpus but contains no Primal prospect and no Primal business. Must not enter any Primal denominator.

Ben discloses concurrent commercial work for another operator and disparages the Primal offer and its buyers to that external audience while labelled '(Primal Instinct)' on the recording: 'Back closing for Boris again. His, I'm like, dude, fitness is annoying to sell, dude. These people suck.' Later: 'I was just selling like a fitness program for 6K ... it's teaching people how to use kettlebells ... Like, I have to, like, pain in the [ass]. But, like, you guys are selling something that makes people money. So it should be, like, infinitely easier to sell.'

He taught the full open-wallet framework verbatim, including the credit-card step and the instruction to direct a prospect's unused limit at the fee: 'what about credit cards? How many credit cards do you have? What's the available balance? And then often you'll find that they have a card with, like, a 20K limit, which is, like, they haven't spent anything. I was like, oh, dude ... why don't we just throw it on a card, go all in.'

A member described a prospect who cried during the meeting, had been struggling for ten years and had zero dollars in the bank, and who was walked down through multiple price points and two Klarna financing applications. Ben's assessment was 'it sounds like you did everything right.'

Credit scores are used as a financing-approval screen and were coached as such: 'generally it's, like, 640 and above is usually around the cutoff of people that'll get approved', with an anecdote about a prospect who paid $9,000 in full on a credit score in the 500s.

Ben's stated sales sequence, which is materially more structured than what he executes on his own Primal calls: facts and figures first, then 'the second half is going to be more of the emotions, decisions, tying them down, getting them into commitment, pre-handling objections'.

He explicitly cross-references the Josh Lyons mastermind session that is also in this batch — a member says 'I was watching the training that you did with Josh Lyons' — confirming both third-party files belong to the same outside sales ecosystem.

Useful counter-pressure content: on a member losing conviction because clients were not getting results, Ben located the cause in the sale itself — 'client success starts in a sales call ... the amount of depth that you go and the amount of commitment that you get that person into, they carry that momentum into working with you and getting the results.'
Ben ran this session between Primal calls and ended it to take one: 'probably have a guy joining my Zoom room here in a minute, so I got to bounce.'
